idiom_name: opaque handle + function-pointer dispatch table over a transport vtable
implementation_notes: C has no classes, so the delegate is an opaque struct: the public header exposes only the handle and a few wrapper functions, while the implementation struct embeds a transport vtable (libcurl easy handle, socket wrapper, in-house RPC ops) plus any cached lookup result, and the wrappers dispatch through it. The LookupService role becomes a resolve() step that fills the handle once (guarded by pthread_once or a mutex) and hands back a reusable handle; exception translation becomes an error-code remapping that must preserve the original errno/transport code for diagnosis. The classic hand-written form is still right when a legacy C transport API (CORBA C bindings, DCE/RPC) must be hidden from application code.
pitfalls: The lookup cache inside the handle is not thread-safe by default; guard it with pthread_once/a mutex, and never share one handle across threads without a lock.
Remapping transport errors to a single code erases retryable-vs-fatal information unless the original errno/transport code is stored and exposed.
The handle owns the connection and any cached strings; skipping svc_close leaks descriptors and buffers.
